verdicts.reason: A: the book cover overlaps the card's left edge, the body copy leaves 'all night.' orphaned on its own line, and the logo, the eyebrow (moved below the body) and the fine print are tiny and unreadable. B has the same row of tiny logo, eyebrow and legal text squeezed beside the CTA and also bleeds the card off the top and bottom of the canvas, but the book clears the card a little better, so its edges are slightly cleaner.

Both are nearly the same layout with the same faults: a tiny logo, unreadable fine print, the eyebrow demoted below the body copy, a small CTA, and the card bleeding off the canvas edges. A keeps the book on the left, so the eye goes from book to headline, close to the original's order. B moves the book to the right, where its edge collides with the card, and leaves a busy empty confetti strip on the left.

A enlarges the eyebrow '24 HOURS, 24 READERS' into a big red line under the body copy, where it competes with the headline and breaks the reading order. A also lets the book overlap the card's right edge and leaves the logo and fine print unreadably small. B keeps the eyebrow subordinate and the book clear of the copy, but its logo and legal text are still illegible and it has an orphaned 'toast all night.' line.

A has the oversized red eyebrow placed under the body copy, where it competes with the headline, plus a book colliding with the card's right edge and an illegible logo and legal line. B keeps a cleaner hierarchy and the book stays separate, though its logo and fine print are still tiny and the card bleeds off the top and bottom of the canvas.
